# Skill: delete-comment

# Delete comments

Audit the requested source scope, including tests and scripts. Preserve the current worktree's unrelated edits. Count comment tokens with a language-aware parser where available; a text search is only a discovery aid.

For each comment, inspect the surrounding code and current tests:

| Class | Test | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Tautology | The code already states the same fact | Delete |
| Stale | The described behavior or name no longer exists | Delete |
| Excuse | The note rationalizes a workaround, swallowed error, or incomplete path | File one concrete repair task with a verify command, then delete the note |
| Decision record | A surprising, costly-to-reverse tradeoff explains the implementation | Record the decision and reason in the repo's existing ADR or decision location, then delete the source comment |

Retain required legal notices, shebangs, generated-file markers, compiler directives, and public API documentation where removing them would change tooling or the published interface. Record these separately from the four cleanup classes. If classification is uncertain, inspect call sites and history before acting.

## Secondary engineering review

While reading each area for comments, use `codebase-design`, `quality-bar`, and `root-cause-not-symptom` where available, plus the repository's relevant language and framework skills. Look for duplicated decisions, shallow modules, tangled ownership, unsafe error handling, weak test seams, avoidable complexity, and measurable performance or reliability problems. Check callers and tests before judging an apparent problem.

Keep comment cleanup as the slice's deliverable. Record only material opportunities in the project's existing issue tracker or backlog, with a code location, evidence of impact, a concrete proposed change, and a verify command. Deduplicate against existing tasks and rank by impact. Implement an unrelated refactor in its own task so the comment diff stays reviewable. A clean area can have no secondary findings.

For `sf-v2`, `bun run check:lint` enforces `scripts/comment-baseline.json`. It rejects new or changed comment text and allows deletions. After a cleanup passes against the old baseline, run `bun scripts/check-comments.ts --update-baseline`, then run the full repository gates. Keep the ratchet moving downward; never refresh it to admit an added comment.

Use small reviewable slices for large repositories. Give each slice its own verify command and dependency edge. Report blocks removed, comment-only physical lines removed, remaining blocks, and the evidence behind any estimate. Land only the files the slice owns.
